note: The 207-byte attacker-controlled CRAM input is copied into a memory hFILE and passed to hts_hopen, which detects the CRAM format and opens it for reading.
Format detection classifies the input as CRAM, so hts_hopen dispatches to cram_dopen, passing the attacker-controlled hFILE.
cram_dopen parses the CRAM file definition and calls cram_read_SAM_hdr to decode the SAM header block, which contains the attacker-controlled compressed data.
cram_read_SAM_hdr reads the container and the first block via cram_read_block, then decompresses it with cram_uncompress_block.
cram_read_block allocates a 2-byte heap buffer b->data (comp_size=2) and fills it with the attacker-controlled compressed block bytes 0x29 0x00.
The block method is RANS_PR0, so cram_uncompress_block passes the 2-byte b->data buffer and comp_size=2 to the rANS decoder.
rans_uncompress_4x16 forwards the 2-byte input buffer (in_size=2) to rans_uncompress_to_4x16.

in[0]=0x29 has the X_STRIPE (0x08) bit set, so the stripe path runs: c_meta_len starts at 1, var_get_u32(in+1,in_end,&ulen) consumes in[1]=0x00 (1 byte) making c_meta_len=2, then in[2] is read from the 2-byte buffer -> heap-buffer-overflow READ 1.
